language: ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English: max 20 words per sentence, one topic per sentence, active voice, simple tenses, no -ing forms, technical names kept as written.

paper.title: Attention Is All You Need
paper.authors: Vaswani, Shazeer, Parmar, Uszkoreit, Jones, Gomez, Kaiser, Polosukhin

episodes.hook: Most AI language models of today use one architecture from a {2017|twenty seventeen} paper.

beats.label: Before 2017: recurrent networks
beats.say: Before {2017|twenty seventeen}, a recurrent network read a sentence one word after the other. It was slow to train on long sentences.

beats.label: The Transformer, 2017
beats.say: The Transformer has no recurrent steps. It uses only attention. It reads all the words of a sentence at the same time.

beats.label: From the paper, Figure 4
beats.say: Attention connects each word to the other words. In this example from the paper, two attention heads connect ‘its’ to ‘Law’.

scene.note: Redrawn from Figure 4: two heads (5 and 6), layer 5 of 6

beats.label: Query, key, value
beats.say: Each word has a query, a key and a value. The model compares the query with all keys. This gives a weight for each value.

scene.note: Weights: illustration, not from the paper

beats.label: English to German, WMT 2014
beats.say: The big Transformer got a BLEU score of 28.4 for English to German translation. This was more than 2 points better than the best previous results. The training time was 3.5 days on 8 GPUs.

episodes.outro: Source: Attention Is All You Need, {2017|twenty seventeen}. The full episode explains each part.

paper.title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training

episodes.hook: In {2018|twenty eighteen}, OpenAI kept only the decoder half of the Transformer.

beats.label: 12 layers, masked self-attention
beats.say: The model has 12 decoder layers. With masked self-attention, each word sees only the words before it.

beats.label: Pre-training objective
beats.say: In pre-training, the model has one task. It predicts the next word from the words before it.

scene.note: Probabilities: illustration, not from the paper

beats.label: BooksCorpus: text with no labels
beats.say: The pre-training text was more than 7,000 unpublished books. The books have long passages, so the model can use information from far back in the text.

beats.label: Stage 2: one task, labeled data
beats.say: Then, fine-tuning adapts the model to each task. Start, delimiter and extract tokens put each task input into one sequence.

scene.note: Redrawn from Figure 1: textual entailment input

beats.label: New best results
beats.say: The model got new best results on 9 of 12 tasks. On Story Cloze, it was 8.9 points better than the previous best.

scene.note: Tables 2–4: previous best (white) vs this paper (yellow) · axis starts at 40

episodes.outro: Source: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training, {2018|twenty eighteen}. Next: BERT reads text in two directions.

paper.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

episodes.hook: GPT reads from left to right. BERT reads in both directions.

beats.label: Bidirectional Transformer encoder
beats.say: BERT uses the Transformer encoder. Each word sees the words on its left and the words on its right.

scene.note: Ep 2, GPT: left side only · BERT: all words

beats.label: Masked language model
beats.say: In pre-training, BERT selects 15 percent of the words. It usually replaces them with a mask token. Then it predicts each word from both sides.

scene.note: Of the selected 15%: replacement rule from Section 3.1

beats.label: Next sentence prediction
beats.say: BERT also gets two sentences, A and B. It predicts if B is the next sentence after A. This is true for 50 percent of the examples.

scene.note: Examples from the paper, Appendix A.1

beats.label: BooksCorpus + English Wikipedia
beats.say: The pre-training text was BooksCorpus and English Wikipedia. Together, they have about 3.3 billion words.

beats.label: New best results on 11 tasks
beats.say: BERT got new best results on eleven tasks. Its GLUE score was 80.5. The score of OpenAI GPT was 72.8.

scene.note: Section 4.1 and Table 1: OpenAI GPT (white) vs BERT-Large (yellow) · axis starts at 40

episodes.outro: Source: BERT, by Devlin and others, {2018|twenty eighteen}. Next: GPT-2 makes the model much larger.

paper.title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
paper.authors: Radford, Wu, Child, Luan, Amodei, Sutskever

episodes.hook: In {2019|twenty nineteen}, GPT-2 did many tasks with no training for them.

beats.label: Largest of 4 model sizes
beats.say: The largest GPT-2 model has 1.5 billion parameters. The smallest model has the same size as GPT-1.

beats.label: 8M+ documents, 40 GB
beats.say: The training text was WebText. It came from Reddit links with at least 3 karma. It has more than 8 million documents.

beats.label: No fine-tuning
beats.say: GPT-2 gets no fine-tuning. The text of the prompt tells the model the task. For example, {TL;DR|T L D R} asks for a summary.

prompts: english sentence = french sentence  …  english sentence =

beats.label: LAMBADA accuracy
beats.say: On LAMBADA, a model predicts the last word of a long passage. GPT-2 increased the accuracy from 19 percent to 52.66 percent.

scene.note: Section 3.3: accuracy of language models on LAMBADA

beats.label: Datasets, zero-shot
beats.say: GPT-2 got new best results on 7 of 8 language modeling datasets. But the largest model still underfits WebText.

episodes.outro: Source: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners, {2019|twenty nineteen}. Next: T5 makes each task text to text.
